Shri Akash Kaushal - Advocate for the objector.

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No.17070/2023, an application filed under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant No.1 Chunnilal @ Ajab Singh Yaduwanshi arising out of judgment dated 21.12.2021 delivered in Sessions Trial No.78/2019 by h 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Hoshangabad.

The appellant No.1 has been convicted under Section 148 of the I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo RI for 1 year with fine of Rs.1000/-, Section 323/149 (six counts) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for six months with fine of Rs. 500 in each count and Section 302/149 of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for life and fine of Rs. 3000/- with default stipulation.
By taking this Court to the prosecution story, learned senior counsel for the appellant No. 1 submits that incident took place at the spur of moment.
The said quarrel unfortunately took an ugly shape.
There was no premeditation.
Necessary ingredients to attract Section 302 of IPC are missing.
Although this appellant has been falsely arraigned as main accused but only lathi has been seized from him.
He further submits that appellant No. 1 remained in custody for near about 4 years and 8 months.
The role allegedly played by this appellant is similar to appellants No. 3 to 6 whose got the benefit of suspension of sentence by order dated 09.09.2022 passed in this appeal.
The final hearing of this matter is not possible in near future.
Thus, remaining jail sentence of present appellant No.1 may be suspended.
The prayer is opposed by learned Government Advocate on the basis of objection but he did not dispute the period of custody and factum of parity.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the objector has also opposed the suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

This Court while granting bail to appellants No. 3 to 6 recorded as under:-
"Learned senior counsel for these appellants by taking this Court to the prosecution story submits that on 25/03/2019 there was a trivial incident of crossing the tractor because of which a quarrel took place which as per prosecution story took a dirty shape.
The deceased Jeevan Singh was assaulted by co-accused Nirbhay Singh and Chhunilal.
Shivam (PW-1), an eye-witness entered the witness box and categorically deposed that the injuries were caused on the person of deceased by Nirbhay Singh and Chhunilal.
The statement of Doctors PW-14 and PW-16 were also relied upon to submit that in fact there is only one injury on the person of deceased because of which he succumbed to death.
Shri Datt, learned senior counsel further pointed out that the incident had taken place on 25/03/2019 and the deceased was hospitalized on 05/06/2019.
He was discharged on 05/06/2019 and died on 07/06/2019.

Further allegation of prosecution is that appellants assaulted other persons also but for those allegations,
the appellants were held guilty for committing offence under Section 323 of the IPC and directed to undergo sentence for a period of six months.
Shri Datt urged that considering the reason of incident, it cannot be said that necessary ingredients for attracting Sections 147 & 148 of the IPC are present.
These appellants were on bail during trial and they did not misuse the liberty.
The final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near further.
These appellants are not the main accused persons who have caused injuries.
The remaining jail sentence of these appellants may be suspended.

The prayer is opposed by learned Government Advocate on the basis of objection and placed reliance on Para-52 of the impugned judgment wherein Court below recorded that it is true that if all the accused would have caused injuries to the deceased Jeevan Singh, multiple injuries would have been there on his person.
Thus, it appears that there is embellishment in the manner accused persons have allegedly assaulted the deceased person.
However, the Court below categorically found that the appellants are guilty by taking aid of Sections 147 & 148 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the objector borrowed the said argument and in addition placed reliance on Para-13 of the impugned judgment wherein number of injuries are shown as five.

Countering the aforesaid, Shri Datt, learned senior counsel placed reliance on the Autopsy Surgeon's statement (PW-16) wherein he deposed about one major injury on the head of the deceased which became reason of death.
Rest of the injuries were bed sores because of long retention of deceased in the ICU.

sentences.text: 2 We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Considering the reason on the streangth of which incident had taken place coupled with the limited role attributed to the present appellants, without expressing any conclusive opinion on the merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of these appellants.
Accordingly, I.A.No. 3616/2022 is allowed"

Considering the factual backdrop, period of actual custody, aspects of parity and bleak chances of final hearing in near future, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of this appellant.
Accordingly, I.A No. 17070/2023, is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of appellant No. 1 is hereby suspended and it is directed that appellant No.1 Chunnilal @ Ajab Singh Yaduwanshi be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, Hoshangabad on 22.01.2024 and also on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SUJOY PAUL) (BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI)
 JUDGE JUDGE  L.R.
